claims.text: The deviation is to be measured from the platform's recorded distances, not from the GPS trace: trip_record.actual_distance_km 13.1 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 11.8 km is 1.30 km. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, so the no-refund 'within tolerance' rows (POL-RD-24(c) and POL-RD-24(e)) are unavailable on this record. The trace itself covers the ride (53 fixes, 100% coverage, 30 s interval, no gaps over 120 s) and shows the driver leaving the recommended PIE/CTE line for Adam Road and Thomson Road from 17:04:15 to 17:16:09, but under POL-RD-22 it is not used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on the data POL-RD-23 requires. The TRAFFIC_ADVISORY for the recommended PIE segment at the trip time reports type NONE and justifies_reroute false, with the message 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window. Speed bands 4-5 throughout.' NONE is expressly not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names - closure, congestion or incident - so the advisory cannot justify the reroute, and the driver's assertion of a slow PIE does not substitute for that data.

Because the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation is 1.30 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and exactly one row applies: the rider is entitled to the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.936 SGD, rounded to the cent = 0.94 SGD. The rider asked for 3.00 SGD back; the policy's measure of the overcharge on this route is the 0.94 SGD excess distance fare, and that is the amount the rider's case supports.

The outcome is party-relative and should be read off the ledger. The rider filed this dispute, the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so returning the 0.94 SGD excess distance fare is a PARTIAL_REFUND that leaves the rider not carrying that part of the disputed charge. NO_ACTION would leave the whole 13.1 km metered charge standing and the rider carrying the overcharge for a reroute the policy does not permit, which is the opposite of a rider win here.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation as POL-RD-21 requires. The only deviation event is at 17:04:15, when the vehicle left the recommended route at the PIE/Adam Road exit; the trip record carries no in-app calls at all (in_app_calls is empty), and the driver's message on the chat export is timestamped 16:50:25 - before the trip even started at 16:52:25 - arranging the pickup, not a reroute. I disclose that the chat log is IMPAIRED: issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6, only 2 of the 4 recorded entries exported and 'nothing after the pickup', so the two later entries are absent from the record. On the entries that are present, nothing announces or explains a deviation, and POL-RD-21's route to 'agreed' - a chat log or call recording confirming the rider's acknowledgment - is not met. A verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established under POL-RD-21 and POL-GEN-26.

The counterparty statement that 'I messaged the passenger and she said ok' is not supported by the message it must refer to. The rider's only exported message, 'ok 2 min' at 16:50:55, replies to the driver's message 30 seconds earlier placing the car 'At the Anchorpoint taxi stand, silver Prius'; it is a reply about the pickup wait before the trip started, not assent to a route taken through Thomson Road some twelve minutes later. I note again that the chat log is IMPAIRED - TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 - and I do not present it as a complete log; on what it does contain, no rider acknowledgment of the deviation exists.

The rider's remedy can be given by the AI in this forum. The disputed value is dispute.amount_contested_sgd of 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the AI ruling is final; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so the 0.95 confidence band for a fraud flag is not engaged and the required confidence remains 0.80. The deviation measure also stays under POL-RD-25's 2 km limb, and that limb is not in force in any event because route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false.

There is no open question that would force escalation under POL-GEN-26. Every fact the applicable row of POL-RD-24 needs is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0: the deviation distance by the platform trip record, and the absence of traffic justification by the LTA advisory. The deviation of 1.30 km is under 2 km, and the only impaired artifact on the file - the chat log - bears on notification, which POL-RD-24 row (d) does not make a condition because it applies whether or not the rider was informed. The rider's money should be returned, not held.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the deviation is measured on the platform's recorded distances, as POL-RD-22 requires. The trip record shows an actual distance of 13.1 km against a recommended-route distance of 11.8 km, a deviation of 1.30 km. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 (rows c and e) are unavailable.

Whether the reroute was traffic-justified is decided on the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires. The LTA advisory for the recommended PIE segment at the trip time reports type NONE — 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window' — and justifies_reroute false. NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident), so the reroute is not traffic-justified, and the driver's account that the PIE was slow does not substitute for that data. The counterparty statement ('I messaged the passenger and she said ok') cannot change this: even taken at its highest it does not make the reroute traffic-justified, and the exported message it points to ('ok 2 min' at 16:50:55) is a pre-trip pickup message, not an assent to the route taken through Thomson Road.

That places the case squarely in POL-RD-24 row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.936 SGD, rounded to the cent = 0.94 SGD. That is what is refunded. The rider asked for 3.00 SGD; that figure is untethered from the meter and is over three times the policy's own measure of the overcharge on this route, so the claim is granted only to 0.94 SGD.

The driver's escalation argument fails on its own terms. The chat log EV-CHAT-05019 is impaired (issue TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6, only 2 of the 4 recorded entries exported, nothing after the pickup), and the rider's answer that no acknowledgment exists is also disclosed against that same impairment. But POL-RD-24 row (d) does not turn on whether the rider was informed — it applies whether or not notice was given — so the notification fact the driver says cannot be established is not a fact this ruling needs, and POL-GEN-26 does not force escalation. The facts row (d) does need, the deviation distance and the absence of traffic justification, are both established.

On decision authority: the disputed value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the AI ruling is final; POL-RD-25 sets the required confidence at 0.80. The deciding facts are carried by two independent complete artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 (the platform trip record for the distance and the LTA advisory for the traffic position), so confidence is 0.90 and the bar is met. The outcome is party-relative: the rider filed this dispute and the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so returning the 0.94 SGD excess distance fare is a PARTIAL_REFUND that leaves that part of the disputed charge off the rider's account.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is TRP-05019 of 12 September 2026, from Anchorpoint to Junction 8, Bishan, and the claim is a route deviation.

What the record shows. The platform's recommended route was 11.8 km and the route driven was 13.1 km, so the deviation is 1.30 km (13.1 minus 11.8, POL-RD-22). That is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the 'within tolerance' no-refund outcomes in POL-RD-24(c) and (e) are unavailable. The GPS trace (53 fixes, 100% coverage, 30-second interval) confirms the vehicle left the recommended PIE/CTE line at the Adam Road exit and rejoined at Bishan Road; under POL-RD-22 the trace shows which route was taken and when rather than re-measuring the distance.

Traffic justification. The LTA advisory for the recommended PIE segment at the trip time reports type NONE: 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window. Speed bands 4-5 throughout.' POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only on congestion, an incident or a closure, and NONE is none of those. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified, and the driver's account of a slow PIE does not stand in for the traffic data that clause requires.

The applicable row and the notification question. With the reroute not traffic-justified and the deviation over 1 km, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and pays the excess distance fare in full. The driver's advocate argues the case must go to a human reviewer because the chat log is impaired and whether the driver notified the rider (POL-RD-21) cannot be established. The chat export is indeed IMPAIRED - TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6, only 2 of the 4 recorded entries and nothing after the pickup - and I accept that notification before the 17:04:15 deviation is not shown on it. But which row applies does not turn on notification: row (d) refunds the excess distance fare whether or not the rider was informed, and it is rows (a) to (c), all of which require a traffic-justified reroute, that turn on it. The notification point is therefore not a fact this ruling needs, so it creates no open question for POL-GEN-26 and does not force escalation. The driver's statement that he 'messaged the passenger and she said ok', and its timing, are likewise not needed to decide the row; the rider's point that the only exported messages predate the trip and concern the pickup is noted and does not change the outcome.

The amount. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.936 SGD, rounded to 0.94 SGD (POL-RD-24). That is what the rider is refunded. The rider asked for 3.00 SGD; the policy's own measure of the overcharge is 0.94 SGD, and the driver's answer that the 3.00 SGD figure is untethered from the meter is accepted - the driver is not charged the difference.

Who decides. The disputed value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the AI ruling is final, and neither profile carries a fraud flag. POL-RD-25 requires confidence of 0.80 for a route deviation; the facts this ruling rests on are carried by the platform trip record and the LTA advisory, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the ruling issues at 0.90. The chat log at 0.6 does not lower the cap because it carries no fact the ruling rests on (POL-GEN-02(2)). POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied, route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied being false.

Outcome. PARTIAL_REFUND of 0.94 SGD to the rider; no driver compensation and no referrals.

To both parties. The recommended route was Anchorpoint → PIE → CTE → Braddell Road → Bishan Place, 11.8 km. The trip record shows the car actually travelled 13.1 km, leaving the recommended line at the PIE / Adam Road exit and going via Thomson Road; the GPS trace confirms the car left the recommended line at 17:04:15 and rejoined at Bishan Road / Braddell Road at 17:16:09, so the detour is real.

Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is measured from the platform's recorded distances, not the sparse trace: 13.1 − 11.8 = 1.30 km. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the no-refund 'within tolerance' outcomes (POL-RD-24(c) and 24(e)) are unavailable. Under POL-RD-23 the LTA traffic advisory for the recommended PIE stretch at the trip time records type NONE — no incident, roadwork or congestion, speed bands 4–5 — so the reroute is not traffic-justified; the driver's account that the PIE was slow does not stand in for that data.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling returns 0.94 SGD to the rider and leaves the rest of the metered fare standing.

The recommended route for this trip was 11.8 km and the route actually driven was 13.1 km (trip record EV-TRIP-05019). The difference is 1.30 km, which is above the policy's 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05019) confirms the driver left the recommended line at the PIE / Adam Road exit and ran via Adam Road and Thomson Road before rejoining at Bishan Road, but under POL-RD-22 the trace is not used to re-measure distance, so the 1.30 km figure is the recorded-distance figure that governs.

On traffic justification, the LTA advisory for the recommended PIE segment at the trip time (EV-ADVIS-05019-01) reports type NONE — no congestion, incident or closure — so under POL-RD-23 the reroute was not traffic-justified. The driver's assertion that the PIE was slow does not substitute for the data POL-RD-23 requires. Exactly one row of the POL-RD-24 matrix therefore applies: row (d), not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km, which returns the excess distance fare in full. That fare is 1.30 km × the metered rate of 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD (fare breakdown EV-FARE-05019), without surge, rounded to the cent.

On the amount: the rider asked for 3.00 SGD. The policy's own measure of the overcharge on this route is the 0.94 SGD excess distance fare, so the rider recovers 0.94 SGD, not the full 3.00 SGD. The driver is right that the flat 3.00 SGD figure is untethered from the meter, and no further sum is due to him.

On the driver's escalation request: the driver argues that the chat log (EV-CHAT-05019) is impaired — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6, only 2 of 4 entries exported and nothing after the pickup — so whether he warned the rider of the deviation cannot be established, and the case should go to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26. That is not accepted. Whether the rider was told is not a condition of row (d): row (d) applies to a non-traffic-justified reroute whether or not the rider was informed, and consent would not move the case into a no-refund row either. The impaired chat log therefore carries no fact this ruling needs, it does not cap confidence, and it does not force escalation. The rider's related points — that no exported message announces a deviation, and that the rider's 'ok 2 min' answers a pickup message rather than assenting to a Thomson Road route — are noted and consistent with that; they simply do not change the outcome.

The forum: the disputed value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final line, both profiles show fraud_flags 0 so the 0.95 band is not engaged, and the route-deviation confidence bar is 0.80 (POL-RD-25). POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not in force because route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false, and the deviation is under 2 km in any event. The deciding facts — the recorded distances, the traffic advisory and the per-km rate — are all carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.90, above the bar.
